# Bootstrapping evie-kit in this repo

This project is configured for the evie-kit toolkit. What arrives
through git: the committed `.claude/skills/*`, the hooks, and
`.evie-kit/settings.*`. What does NOT: the toolkit itself —
`node_modules/@evie-kit/*` is a machine-local link. A fresh clone
therefore has instructions that name commands it does not yet have.

**`bun install` is not enough.** This repo deliberately declares no
`@evie-kit` dependency (the bare name resolves to an unrelated
public package — a dependency-confusion risk), so the standard install
gesture succeeds while leaving the toolchain absent.

## First run on a new machine

1. Get an evie-kit checkout — anywhere you like, but see the
   stability note below.
   `git clone 'git@github.com:evie-platform/evie-kit.git'
   ~/src/evie-kit`, then `bun install --frozen-lockfile` inside the
   checkout (frozen, so a newer bun cannot rewrite its lockfile and
   dirty the checkout — copies stamped from a dirty checkout can never
   be proven current).
2. Bootstrap THIS repo from that checkout, **by path** — the linked
   `evie-kit` command does not exist yet, which is why the first
   invocation cannot use it:

   ```bash
   # from the root of THIS repo; substitute your own checkout path
   bun /path/to/evie-kit/packages/cli/src/evie-kit.ts onboard
   ```

3. From then on, the linked path works from inside this repo:

   ```bash
   bun node_modules/@evie-kit/cli/src/evie-kit.ts <verb>
   ```

`onboard` is the right verb here: it joins an ALREADY-configured repo
and writes only machine-local things (the link, your credentials,
per-machine tool config). Do not run `evie-kit setup` in this repo —
setup configures a repo for the first time and writes committed files
that are already committed here.

## Sharp edges

- **Module-not-found means an un-run bootstrap, not a broken repo.** If
  `bun node_modules/@evie-kit/cli/...` dies with module-not-found,
  step 2 has not run on this machine. The committed skills are correct;
  the toolchain is missing.
- **Keep the checkout where you put it.** The location is yours to
  choose, but moving it later breaks the `bun link` registration:
  re-run onboard (or `bun link` in the checkout's `packages/cli`)
  after a move.
- **Every goal worktree needs the link too.** A worktree under
  `.worktrees/` is a fresh checkout of this repo, and the link is
  machine-local per checkout — provisioning does not wire it, and
  promotion moves the worktree one level (a RELATIVE link dangles).
  Module-not-found inside a worktree is the same un-run bootstrap:
  run step 2 by path from inside that worktree.
- **Agents: the toolkit's own docs carry your reading order.** The
  evie-kit checkout's `docs/llms.txt` is the agent entry-point index
  (reading order, the authority rule, the setup entry). Your operating
  contracts are the skills under `.claude/skills/` here; when a guide
  page and a skill disagree, the skill wins.
- **The copies here are FROZEN; the linked code is not.** The skills and
  hooks above arrived through git at whatever moment setup last ran,
  while `node_modules/@evie-kit/*` is whatever the linked checkout is
  today. `.evie-kit/state/copies.json` records which evie-kit produced
  each of them, and a session that starts against stale copies says so.
  To ask at any time:

  ```bash
  bun node_modules/@evie-kit/cli/src/evie-kit.ts copies check
  ```

  `evie-kit upgrade` re-copies the MANAGED artifacts and re-stamps
  them. Your `.evie-kit/settings.*` is not one of them: setup
  scaffolded it once and it is yours now, so its stamp is provenance
  only — skew in its SHAPE surfaces through the settings loader's own
  deprecation errors instead.
- **Access is part of the bootstrap.**
  The evie-kit repo may be private, and a 404 while cloning is
  indistinguishable from a typo — so if the clone fails, ask whoever
  configured this repo (whoever ran `evie-kit setup` here) rather than
  retrying the URL.
- **Orchestrator sessions record their seat (EVA-212).**
  Two supervising sessions exist here (ADR 0022): a PLANNER, which
  drafts and grills goals and never records itself, and ONE ORCHESTRATOR
  per project, which launches executors, receives lock reports and lands
  merges. Only when the user designates THIS session as the
  orchestrator, run `bun node_modules/@evie-kit/cli/src/evie-kit.ts
  goals bind orchestrator` once at the start of the session to record
  its seat — every goal it launches phones its lock report home to that
  seat. An orchestrator started with `goals spawn orchestrator` is
  recorded already and needs no bind. Load the `goals` skill for the
  lifecycle either way.
- **House prose style binds every session.**
  House prose style: write every piece of prose in this repository by
  `.evie-kit/conventions/writing-style.md` (the tracked house voice)
  plus its gitignored addendum
  `.evie-kit/conventions/writing-style.local.md`, which wins on
  contradiction; read both at every writing seam (drafting, review
  gates, tracker comments, handoffs). Lint tuning lives in settings,
  never in that pair.
